### Summary

Chemistry enters the two-dimensional solver as source terms: each term gives, in every cell, a tendency
$S(c)$ and its Jacobian $\partial S / \partial c$. The implicit steps of @sec-ch09-rosenbrock and @sec-ch09-newton
only ever need this pair. Sources come from three places: kintera's kinetics and photochemistry modules
(@sec-ch06, @sec-ch07), whose reaction Jacobians are mapped to species; a set of simple built-in sources (first-order
loss, mass action, reversible exchange, boundary fluxes); and any user object that follows the same protocol.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Per-cell $S$ and $\partial S/\partial c$, summed over terms, @eq-ch09-sources-sum.

**Data.** `(ncol, nlyr, nspecies)` tendency, `(ncol, nlyr, nspecies, nspecies)` Jacobian; rates in the caller's units.

**Placement.** Linearized once per stage or Newton iteration, at the current state.

**Activation.** `source_terms=[...]` of the step functions; `kinetics=`, `photo_chem=` of `build_implicit_operator`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Analytic Jacobians; reactant concentrations clamped at 0 inside the built-in sources.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $S_n$, the source of species $n$ in a cell [concentration time$^{-1}$]; $\mathsf J$, the per-cell
Jacobian $\partial S/\partial c$; $k$, a rate or rate constant; $\nu_{nr}$, net stoichiometric coefficient of species
$n$ in reaction $r$; $\mathsf R$, the reaction-space Jacobian of @sec-ch06.

### Derivation

Each term $t$ returns its tendency and Jacobian in every cell, and the solver adds them:

$$
\begin{aligned}
S &= \sum_t S^{(t)}(c), \\
\mathsf J &= \sum_t \frac{\partial S^{(t)}}{\partial c} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-sources-sum}

@eq-ch09-sources-sum is formed in `build_source_linearization`
({{< code python/atm2d/sources/combine.py build_source_linearization >}}). A term may also supply a non-local
operator (`global_operator`), which `build_source_global_operator` sums into a sparse matrix.

For kintera's kinetics, the species Jacobian is the reaction Jacobian mapped through the stoichiometry,

$$
\mathsf J_{nm} = \sum_r \nu_{nr}\, \mathsf R_{rm} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-sources-stoich}

computed in `build_chemistry_jacobian` ({{< code python/atm2d/chemistry.py build_chemistry_jacobian >}}) from
`kinetics.forward` and `kinetics.jacobian`, and likewise for photochemistry in `build_photochemistry_jacobian`.

The built-in mass-action source of reactants $a$ with coefficients $p_a$ has rate $w = k \prod_a c_a^{p_a}$; it adds
$+q_b w$ to each product $b$ and $-p_a w$ to each reactant, and its Jacobian column for reactant $m$ is
$k\, p_m c_m^{p_m - 1} \prod_{a \ne m} c_a^{p_a}$ times the same coefficients. A first-order source is the case of one
reactant with $p = 1$; a boundary flux $\Phi$ at the bottom or top cell adds $\pm \Phi / \Delta x_1$ to that cell; a
boundary velocity $v$ adds $\pm (v / \Delta x_1)\, c$.

### Numerical method

Every term is linearized at the current concentration; nothing is iterated inside a term. In the built-in sources the
reactant concentrations are clamped at zero before the rate and its derivatives are formed (`IndexedMassActionSource`,
{{< code python/atm2d/sources/indexed.py IndexedMassActionSource >}}). When a charge-balance pair (cations, electron)
is given, the Jacobian column of the electron is added to every cation column (@sec-ch09-conservation).

The actinic flux that photochemistry needs can be computed by `compute_actinic_flux_disort`
({{< code python/atm2d/radiation.py compute_actinic_flux_disort >}}): the total photoabsorption cross section of each
species (branch 0 of each photolysis reaction) times its number density gives the extinction, times the layer
thickness gives the optical depth; pydisort returns the mean intensity at levels, which is averaged to cell centres and
multiplied by $4\pi$.

The sources figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of the source terms. {#tbl-ch09-sources-code}

Setup checks a user can hit: a term whose tendency or Jacobian has the wrong shape; a rate profile not shaped
`(ncol, nlyr)`; a boundary other than `lower` or `upper`; non-positive vertical cell widths; `photo_chem` without
`actinic_flux`; a photolysis reaction with more than one absorber; a concentration unit other than `mol_m3` or
`molecules_cm3`.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_atm2d.py` (`test_implicit_operator_adds_chemistry_and_photochemistry`) | the operator differs from transport alone when chemistry is added | inequality | qualitative |
| `test_atm2d.py` (`test_implicit_operator_adds_local_source_terms`) | source Jacobians land on the diagonal blocks | default | PyTorch defaults |
| `test_atm2d.py` (`test_mass_action_jacobian_keeps_first_order_zero_reactant_derivative`) | the Jacobian of a first-order term stays $k$ at zero concentration | default | PyTorch defaults |
| `test_atm2d.py` (`test_total_cross_section_uses_absorption_branch_only`) | only branch 0 enters the extinction | exact | equality |
| `test_atm2d.py` (`test_actinic_flux_from_disort_supports_2d_state`) | the actinic flux runs on a 2-D state | shape | construction |

: Tests of the source terms. {#tbl-ch09-sources-tests}

The tolerances are read from `tests/test_atm2d.py` at the pin. No test compares @eq-ch09-sources-stoich with a
finite-difference Jacobian of a kintera network: missing evidence.

### Limits

Clamping reactants at zero makes the linearization exact only for non-negative states; a negative iterate is treated
as zero in the rate but is not itself corrected here (the steps of @sec-ch09-rosenbrock and @sec-ch09-newton clip
afterwards). The optical depth multiplies a number density in cm$^{-3}$ by the layer thickness in the state's own
length unit (verified by reading `compute_actinic_flux_disort`); the caller must make the cross sections and the
thickness consistent, and that a mismatch gives a wrong flux silently is a hypothesis, not run.
